headlines.title: Anthropic’s Dario and Daniela Amodei to join CNBC exclusively from the Nasdaq: IPO live updates
headlines.summary: Anthropic IPO live updates: Follow ANT stock's Nasdaq debut, opening share price, valuation and investor reaction to the Claude AI maker.
headlines.article_text: Anthropic IPO live updates: ANT stock price and Nasdaq debut Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 5:16 05:16 Anthropic raises $81B+ in historic IPO: Here's what to know Squawk Box Anthropic is set for its long-awaited Nasdaq debut on Thursday, after the artificial intelligence lab raised over $81 billion in a record IPO , surpassing SpaceX 's offering in June. The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. Its fully diluted market cap sits at around $1.5 trillion. Tune in at 10:00 a.m. ET as Dario and Daniela Amodei join CNBC TV exclusively to talk about the debut. Watch in real time on CNBC+ or the CNBC Pro stream The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. The company will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT," and its debut will be a big test for the AI industry. Investors have been fretting over Jensen Huang's sudden ouster at Nvidia , voters' stinging rebuke of AI during the midterm elections and the feasibility of a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout . "Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort." Highlights so far: Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace frontier AI development Retail demand for ANT was the largest in history Anthropic employees set to get rich Dario and Daniela Amodei arrive at the Nasdaq CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. 1 Min Ago Anthropic executives wear "Clawd" pins to ring opening bell A pin worn by CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei inside the Nasdaq MarketSite ahead of the anticipated IPO of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in New York City on November 19, 2026. Charly Triballeau | Afp | Getty Images Anthropic executives were sporting "Clawd" pins while they rang the opening bell at the Nasdaq. Clawd is a pixelated crab mascot that the company associates with Claude Code, its popular AI coding product. — Ashley Capoot 22 Min Ago Brad Gerstner: Anthropic not a 'get-rich-quick scheme' watch now VIDEO 8:16 08:16 Brad Gerstner on $5B Anthropic investment: A cornerstone investment for Altimeter Squawk Box Brad Gerstner, founder and CEO of Altimeter Captial, said Anthropic's ability to disprove profitability concerns and make their market debut despite recent headwinds and market pressures facing the tech industry demonstrated how "extraordinary" the company is. "I think this level of demand for the company from Altimeter and others, and from retail investors getting in the game, getting their shot on goal the first time, is real evidence of just how extraordinary this company has operated," Gerstner told CNBC's "Squawk Box." Gerstner's Altimeter Capital is planning on investing $5 billion in the AI lab, which he called a "cornerstone" investment for his firm. "This isn't a get-rich-quick scheme. As I've said, this will be a cornerstone investment for Altimeter. This is a multi-year compounder in the most important super cycle in the history of technology," Gerstner told CNBC. — Caleigh Keating 31 Min Ago Amodei renews pledge to pace the development of AI in Nasdaq speech watch now VIDEO 5:14 05:14 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace the development of AI in Nasdaq speech Squawk on the Street Amodei is speaking about AI's potential benefits and risks in his address at the Nasdaq. He opened by talking about the technology's potential to advance medicine and cure diseases, and he reiterated the company's pledge to focus on safety pace the raining and advancement of AI systems. "Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing," Amodei said. "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same." — Ashley Capoot 38 Min Ago Daniela Amodei's message to people who fear AI Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic speaks inside the Nasdaq MarketSite ahead of the anticipated IPO of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in New York City on November 19, 2026. Charly Triballeau | Afp | Getty Images Daniela Amodei spoke from the Nasdaq ahead of the opening bell, and had a message for people who are scared of AI. "This technology needs you — not your trust, not your use, but your voice," she said. "The end of this story isn't written yet. Intelligence is now something humans can build. What we choose to build with it is up to all of us." —Chris Eudaily 1 Hour Ago Retail demand for Anthropic's IPO was largest in history, sources tell CNBC watch now VIDEO 8:11 08:11 David Faber, CNBC insiders on what to watch from the Anthropic IPO today Squawk Box Retail demand for Anthropic's IPO was larger than demand for any other deal in history, sources told CNBC's David Faber. Anthropic targeted retail allocation of about 20%, as CNBC previously reported, a much higher percentage than the typical initial public offering, which is 5% to 10% for retail investors. Anthropic's stock could trade into the low $100s on Thursday, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. — Ashley Capoot 1 Hour Ago Over 400 Anthropic employees set to become centimillionaires watch now VIDEO 2:18 02:18 Anthropic's IPO could mint thousands of millionaires — and reshape San Francisco Tech The average Anthropic employee will be worth over $40 million after today's IPO, marking one of the most rapid wealth creation events in history. The AI lab has generated 1.77 billion employee options. Earlier hires stand to benefit even further, with over 400 employees expected to be worth $100 million or more at the current share price. Lockup periods may alter the timeline for the gains to make it to the economy, but the newfound wealth is expected to supercharge the San Francisco real estate market and philanthropic giving. — Robert Frank, Caleigh Keating 1 Hour Ago Here's what it's like outside the Nasdaq Outside the Nasdaq ahead of the Anthropic IPO on Nov. 19th, 2026. Ashley Capoot | CNBC As of around 8:00 a.m. ET, the scene outside the Nasdaq is pretty sleepy, though there is some police presence. The Nasdaq isn't promoting Anthropic's logo yet, but there are some ads for Elon Musk's Grok Bot and the neocloud Nebius . — Ashley Capoot 2 Hours Ago Amodeis arrive at the Nasdaq Dario Amodei, chief executive officer of Anthropic PBC, and his wife Camilla Clark arrive for the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images Daniela Amodei, co-founder and president of Anthropic PBC, arrives for the Anthropic PBC initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Data storage name Everpure also got a boost after it lifted its fiscal-year outlook. Follow along as CNBC covers the biggest stock market moves of the day. 4 Min Ago Coherent shares rise after $2 billion buyback authorization The New York Stock Exchange welcomes Coherent Corp. (NYSE: COHR) in celebration of its first anniversary of its acquisition of Coherent, Inc., and three months since it transitioned to the New York Stock Exchange. NYSE Shares of Coherent are up nearly 11%, extending gains after Nvidia 's latest earnings report earlier in the week highlighted continued demand for data-center technology. Coherent -YTD Coherent, which supplies optical components used in AI data centers, said its data-center revenue rose 85% year over year in its fiscal first quarter. On Nov. 18, the company's board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $2 billion . Coherent may buy shares in the open market or through other transactions. The program has no expiration date and does not require the company to repurchase a specific amount. — Deena Zaidi 25 Min Ago Synopsys shares jump Shares of the software company making tools for computer chips jumped 3.2% after Barclays initiated coverage with an overweight rating and a $640 price target implying 47% upside from Wednesday's close. Analyst Saket Kalia noted that Synopsys is the leader of a growing Electronic Design Automation (EDA) market, which is driven by rising spend in semiconductor research and development. Synopsys — Sarah Min 1 Hour Ago UBS upgrades MongoDB MongoDB gained 4% before the bell following an upgrade at UBS to buy from neutral. The bank's channel checks pointed to steady demand and better-than-expected consumer and partner growth, which should support durable 20%-plus total revenue growth and 25%-plus revenue growth for its cloud database service Atlas over the coming years, analyst Radi Sultan said. In addition, MongoDB could be utilized in 20% to 40% of incremental AI workloads, which is not fully reflected in the stock's valuation, he said. — Michelle Fox 1 Hour Ago Data storage stocks surge early Thursday Data storage stocks are getting a lift in the premarket Thursday as the Anthropic IPO aims to breathe new life into AI-trade Shares of Seagate Technology are up more than 6% while Western Digital stock popped 5.8%. Seagate and Western Digital provide provide mass data storage infrastructure, a crucial role in the AI ecosystem to help AI models run. The strong momentum around data storage and AI infrastructure demand is already high. But a large chuck of that demand will come from leading AI lab Anthropic, which is set to go public Thursday. — Paulina Likos 2 Hours Ago Chipmakers advance ahead of Anthropic highly anticipated IPO Chipmakers advanced on Thursday ahead of Anthropic's IPO. Marvell gained 4.2%, Advanced Micro Devices is up 2.8%, Broadcom advanced 2.5%, Intel moved 4.4% higher and Nvidia is up 1.5%. These artificial intelligence chips will help Anthropic run Claude models faster. Leading chipmakers need the IPO to go well, as Anthropic has $900 billion in spending commitments. — Paulina Likos 2 Hours Ago BMO Capital Markets upgrades Bloom Energy, decreases price target Shares of Bloom Energy surged nearly 8% in the premarket Thursday after being upgraded to outperform at BMO Capital Markets. The analysts cited their endorsement of the company after coming away with positive meetings with management. The firm however decreased its price target to $230 from $260, which still implies a 35% upside to the stock's Thursday close of $170 per share. 2 Hours Ago Box shares rise on upgrade UBS upgraded the intelligent content management provider to buy from neutral, sending shares 3.6% higher in premarket trading. The firm believes Box 's recent artificial intelligence growth acceleration can support sustained double-digit revenue growth. "Investors have been looking for evidence that AI can drive an inflection in software growth, and Box is increasingly demonstrating exactly that," analyst Taylor McGinnis wrote. — Michelle Fox 3 Hours Ago Walmart wavers despite earnings beat, outlook increase Walmart shares were down more than 1% even after the retail giant reported third-quarter results that beat expectations and raised its full-year guidance. The company posted adjusted earnings per share of 65 cents on revenue of $188.84 billion. Analysts expected a profit of 64 cents per share on revenue of $187.27 billion. For the year, Walmart sees net sales rising 4.9% to 5.2%, more than a previous guidance of 4% to 5%.
